notes: The Ghostscript flaw itself: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 (fixed upstream 2026-09-08, public ID 2026-11-09). A distribution may carry the fix under an older version number, so read the package changelog. Second source: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125396

WordPress core: an Author or higher account could get code run on the server through a malicious upload when Imagick and Ghostscript are in use. Fixed in 7.0.4 with backports to older branches; cPanel lists 6.8.8, 6.9.7 and 7.0.4. Our note: this is the application-side fix and it does not replace updating Ghostscript. Second source: https://support.cpanel.net/hc/en-us/articles/45216747700503-Security-CVE-2026-125396-Ghostscript-Upload2Shell

Roundcube: versions before 1.6.20 (and 1.7.x before 1.7.5) passed unsafe attachment content to ImageMagick when resizing images. Roundcube's release note describes the fix and Plesk ties this CVE to it. Second source: https://support.plesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/45221939870871-Vulnerability-CVE-2026-125396-and-CVE-2026-114727-Upload2Shell-Remote-code-execution-via-image-processing-in-Roundcube-shipped-with-Plesk-for-Linux

The researchers' test files were PostScript saved under a trusted name (.pdf, .png or .jpg), and their Roundcube attachment was declared image/jpeg. Our note: %!PS is the usual first line of a PostScript file. Other bytes or a comment can come first, and genuine PDFs can embed font data that contains it, so search files with image names (jpg, jpeg, png) before PDFs

The researchers report that image libraries reached Ghostscript with EPS content even when the file was named .png. Our note: %!PS-Adobe is the usual first line of an EPS file. A match in a file with an image name is worth a look; it is not proof of an attack

value: Ghostscript (gs) started with -dSAFER by a web server or mail account (for example www-data) or the print service account (lp)
notes: In the researchers' tests the rendering process ran as www-data (web and Roundcube), lp (CUPS) and roundcube_sysuser (Plesk). Starting Ghostscript this way is normal for thumbnails and print jobs: look for it at odd times, in odd numbers, or with an odd parent process

value: A shell or other program started by a Ghostscript process
notes: The researchers' proofs ran a command as the renderer's own account. Our note: Ghostscript has no ordinary reason to start a shell, so a child process of gs that is a shell or a downloader deserves a close look. The source gives no log signature for it

Where cPanel's temporary measure lives. It adds policy lines that disable the gs delegate and the PS, PS2, PS3, EPS, PDF and XPS coders, and warns it can break previews and thumbnails. Check what your file says. We have not tested the lines and cannot say they are enough

value: A shared print queue reachable from untrusted networks that accepts jobs without a login
notes: The researchers' Debian 13 proof sent a print job to a shared CUPS queue that accepted jobs without authentication and ran a command as lp. They report that requiring authentication on the queue blocked the anonymous submission

value: An ImageMagick policy that lets PostScript EPS or PDF files through to Ghostscript on a server that handles uploads or mail
notes: The Roundcube and DokuWiki proofs needed a permissive ImageMagick setting. A file named like a photo is handed to Ghostscript when ImageMagick judges its contents to be PostScript. Read your policy file (see the policy.xml row)

value: A WordPress site that uses Imagick and Ghostscript and has accounts that can upload files (Author or higher)
notes: WordPress describes the weakness as Author-plus remote code execution through a malicious upload on sites that use Imagick and Ghostscript. Both conditions must hold. Reading who holds upload rights and whether Imagick is installed tells you if the setup exists

A WordPress plugin the researchers tested (version 1.55.1) with a public PDF upload field that stores files in the Media Library, which let a signed-out visitor reach the renderer. The weakness is in Ghostscript, not in this plugin: the entry marks an exposed upload form to review, not a bad plugin

A WordPress plugin the researchers tested (Lite 6.7.0 with Elementor 4.2.0): a public registration widget with a custom upload field let a signed-out visitor reach the renderer when registration was enabled. The weakness is in Ghostscript, not in this plugin: the entry marks an exposed upload form to review

value: A copy of Ghostscript bundled inside a container image or application package
notes: AlmaLinux says containers and application bundles carry their own copy, so updating the host does not update them. pwn.ai makes the same point and adds that a document worker can keep using vulnerable code after the host package changes

value: A service that loaded the Ghostscript library before the update and has not been restarted since
notes: AlmaLinux says long-running services that have the Ghostscript library loaded keep using the old copy until they are restarted, and that its needs-restarting command lists them. Commands that start gs fresh pick up the fix on their next run
AlmaLinux 8 fixed package (production repositories from 2026-11-23); install this or higher. The same version applies to the libgs subpackage
AlmaLinux 9 fixed package (production repositories from 2026-11-23); install this or higher. The same version applies to the libgs subpackage
